The image presents two bar charts, one for Deutschland (Germany) and one for the EU, comparing the percentage of three metals - Aluminium, Kupfer (Copper), and Nickel - over three years: 2021, 2022, and 2023. 

The charts display the data for each metal across the three years, with the x-axis listing the metals and the y-axis representing the percentage. The bars are color-coded to represent the different years: blue for 2021, purple for 2022, and grey for 2023. 

In the Deutschland chart, the percentage of Aluminium decreased from 3.6% in 2021 to 1.0% in 2023, while Kupfer increased from 8.3% in 2021 to 11.3% in 2022 before dropping to 2.2% in 2023. Nickel remained relatively stable, with 25.1% in 2021, 24.7% in 2022, and 11.4% in 2023. 

The EU chart shows a similar trend, with Aluminium decreasing from 3.2% in 2021 to 1.7% in 2023, Kupfer increasing from 4.4% in 2021 to 5.1% in 2022 before dropping to 1.3% in 2023, and Nickel remaining relatively stable, with 24.3% in 2021, 23.3% in 2022, and 14.6% in 2023. 

The charts provide a clear visual representation of the changes in the percentage of these metals over the three-year period, allowing for easy comparison between Deutschland and the EU.
